results.content: This paper is cited as a key related work that also tackles the KV cache bottleneck. KIVI's authors reference FlexGen's use of 4-bit group-wise quantization for both key and value caches, positioning their own asymmetric quantization strategy as a more nuanced and effective approach for lower bit-rates. [...] Large Language Models (LLMs) face significant memory challenges during inference, particularly from the Key-Value (KV) cache that stores intermediate attention states. This cache prevents redundant computation during auto-regressive text generation but can consume terabytes of memory for large batch sizes and long contexts, often exceeding the model parameters themselves. The KV cache creates a bottleneck that limits inference throughput and increases serving costs. [...] This paper's findings are fundamental to the core hypothesis of KIVI. The authors of KIVI explicitly state that their observation of persistent, large-magnitude outliers in fixed channels of the key cache aligns with previous findings in the AWQ paper, providing a critical justification for their decision to quantize the key cache per-channel.

results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache [Quick Review]
results.content:
KIVI quantizes key cache per-channel and value cache per-token based on extensive analysis of outlier patterns and quantization error in KV cache.
 KIVI is a plug-and-play 2-bit KV cache quantization algorithm with hardware-friendly implementation that does not require fine-tuning.
 KIVI incorporates a grouped key cache and a residual key cache, maintaining the residual portion in full precision to handle streaming data and ensure accuracy. [...] KIVI provides a hardware-friendly implementation by fusing dequantization with matrix multiplication using CUDA and implementing group-wise quantization in Triton. [...] Efficiently serving large language models necessitates batching many requests, yet increased batch sizes and context lengths make KV cache a significant memory and speed bottleneck.
 Quantization can reduce KV cache size, but a lack of in-depth studies exists on its element distribution, hindering effective quantization strategies.
 This research aims to analyze KV cache element distribution in LLMs to identify optimal quantization approaches and overcome current limitations.

results.title: The KV Cache Wars? - by Ken Huang - Agentic AI
results.content: The KV cache solves this by storing those key and value projections in memory so they never need to be recomputed. This is the right trade — swapping compute cost for memory cost. But the trade has limits. The KV cache grows linearly with context length, linearly with the number of transformer layers, linearly with batch size, and linearly with the number of key-value heads. At a 128K context window on a 70B-parameter model, that linear growth adds up to roughly 42 gigabytes of KV cache memory [...] is prohibitively expensive at scale.
